data.title: Eagle Capital Growth Fund Declares Year-End Distribution of $0.49 Per Share
data.description:
The Eagle Capital Growth Fund, Inc. (“Fund”) (NYSE American: GRF) today declared a year-end distribution of $0.49 per share in cash. The record date for this distribution is November 27, 2026, and the payment date is December 17, 2026.

On a preliminary basis, this distribution represents a combination of net investment income of $0.055 per share and long-term capital gains of $0.435 per share. All of the net investment income consists of “qualified” dividends. This preliminary information is subject to change. Shareholders will receive definitive information with respect to U.S. Federal income tax treatment. In addition, shareholders can access definitive tax information by going to the Fund’s website after year-end.

The Fund is a closed-end investment company that invests primarily in high-quality growth companies. To learn more about the Fund, please go the Fund’s website: www.eaglecapitalgrowthfund.com

If you have a question about the year-end distribution or other Fund matter, please contact David C. Sims, the Fund’s Chief Financial Officer and Chief Compliance Officer, at (414) 765-1107, or by e-mail to: dave@simscapital.com

data.title: Why are SpiceJet flights being cancelled across India? Financial crisis, airport dues and crew shortages explained
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- SpiceJet is facing mounting operational challenges, with frequent flight cancellations and delays across the country reportedly linked to its worsening financial condition, unpaid airport dues and a shortage of crew members.

According to a report by The New Indian Express, airport authorities have restricted the financially distressed airline's operations over its inability to pay mandatory charges for using airport facilities and services.

The airline has been operating under a 'Cash and Carry' arrangement for airport charges, which requires it to clear payments before availing of services. The Civil Aviation Ministry had permitted this arrangement for SpiceJet for an extended period because of its financial difficulties, The New Indian Express reported, citing an airport source.

Airport charges cover various services provided to aircraft, including Route Navigation Charges and Terminal Navigation Landing Charges.

A senior Airports Authority of India (AAI) official said these charges depend on factors such as the aircraft's weight and the distance travelled.

The airline has reportedly struggled to clear these mandatory payments, creating difficulties in maintaining regular flight operations.

According to the report, SpiceJet has also been unable to pay the Passenger Service Fee (PSF), which is collected from passengers to fund airport facilities and services, including drinking water, toilets and security arrangements involving deployed personnel.

The payment difficulties have added to the airline's operational challenges at major airports.

Apart from financial liabilities to airport authorities, delayed salary payments have reportedly contributed to a shortage of employees.

The airline has not paid salaries to its employees for nearly four months, according to The New Indian Express. The situation has reportedly resulted in high employee attrition, while a shortage of crew members has further affected flight operations.

On September 19, four SpiceJet flights scheduled to depart from Delhi airport could not take off after employees reportedly refused to report for duty over non-payment of their dues.

The shortage of operational staff has made it increasingly difficult for the airline to maintain its scheduled services, resulting in cancellations and delays.

The airline's limited operational fleet has further compounded its difficulties.

According to the media report, only 12 of SpiceJet's 60 aircraft were operational as of Wednesday.

The frequent cancellation of SpiceJet flights has also raised concerns among tourism stakeholders, particularly in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

The Indian Association of Tour Operators (IATO) approached Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu on Tuesday, seeking government intervention over repeated cancellations of SpiceJet flights to Sri Vijayapuram airport, formerly known as Port Blair.

In a letter to the minister, the association said the disruptions were affecting tourism in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where air connectivity plays a crucial role in bringing visitors to the archipelago.

SpiceJet's Board of Directors is scheduled to meet on November 18 to consider and approve a proposal to raise fresh capital, the airline said in a regulatory filing.

The development comes as the budget carrier continues to face significant financial and operational challenges, which have led to a reduction in its flight operations.

"Board of Directors of the Company is scheduled to be held on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, inter-alia, to consider and approve the proposal for raising of fresh capital," the airline said.

The fresh capital could be raised "by way of issuance of equity shares, preference shares, debt securities and/or other permissible instruments, through preferential issue, qualified institutions placement or any other mode," it said.

data.title: Seritage Growth Properties Reports Third Quarter 2026 Operating Results
data.description:
Seritage Growth Properties () (the “Company”), a national owner and developer of retail, residential and mixed-use properties today reported financial and operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

“Although we have no new transactions under contract, we continue to work on both individual asset sales and potential strategic options for the portfolio and the Company,” said Adam Metz, CEO & President.

Q3 Sale Highlights:

  • Generated gross proceeds of $3.0 million from the sale of one vacant/non-income producing asset and received a distribution of $8.9 million from an unconsolidated entity as a result of the sale of a portion of the underlying property.

  • As previously disclosed, the Company has entered into an option purchase and sale agreement (the “PSA”) to sell one vacant non-income producing premier asset in Dallas, Texas for anticipated gross proceeds of $50.8 million before applicable credits and costs. The sale is subject to customary closing conditions and is also cross-conditioned and cross-defaulted with an option purchase and sale agreement between the buyer and unaffiliated owners of a neighboring parcel. The buyer made an initial option payment of $169,200, then (i) commencing on July 1, 2026, and each month thereafter that the PSA remains in effect through December 1, 2026, the Company shall receive an option payment equal to $126,900 and (ii) commencing on January 1, 2027, and each month thereafter that the PSA remains in effect through January 1, 2028, the Company shall receive an option payment equal to $274,950. All option payments are incremental to the purchase price and are non-refundable except as otherwise provided for in the PSA. There can be no assurances that the buyer will exercise the option to purchase the property. The Company has received $0.6 million of option payments through September 30, 2026.

Financial Highlights:

For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026:

  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash on hand of $45.4 million, including $32.7 million of restricted cash, as well as $10.0 million of availability under its revolving loan facility discussed below. As of November 12, 2026, the Company had cash on hand of $41.4 million, including $32.7 million of restricted cash, and $10.0 million of availability under its revolving loan facility.

  • During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company invested $1.9 million and $2.8 million, respectively, in its consolidated properties and $0.3 million and $2.8 million, respectively, in its unconsolidated properties.

  • During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company received distributions of $10.4 million and $19.2 million, respectively, from its unconsolidated properties.

  • The Company did not recognize any impairment charges on its consolidated properties for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The Company recognized an impairment charge of $15.2 million on one of its consolidated properties during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

  • During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company did not record any other-than-temporary impairment losses on its unconsolidated entities. The Company recorded an other-than-temporary impairment loss of $5.2 million on one of its unconsolidated entities during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

  • The Company reported net income attributable to common shareholders of $2.7 million, or $0.05 per share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and a net loss attributable to common shareholders of ($36.2) million, or ($0.64) per share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

  • On July 24, 2026, the Company entered into a new $15.0 million term loan facility and a $25.0 million revolving loan facility. At closing, the Company drew $15.0 million under the revolving loan facility, leaving $10.0 million available for future borrowings. The Company used a combination of the proceeds from the closing of the new loans together with cash on hand to fully repay the $50.0 million outstanding balance on its prior term loan facility.

The Company expects to use existing cash on hand and its availability under the revolving loan facility to pay for its financing obligations and fund its operations and development activity. For more information on our liquidity position, including our going concern analysis, please see the notes to the consolidated financial statements included in Part I, Item 1 and in the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations,” each in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

Litigation Matters

On July 1, 2024, a purported shareholder of the Company filed a class action lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, captioned Zhengxu He, Trustee of the He & Fang 2005 Revocable Living Trust v. Seritage Growth Properties, Case No. 1:24:CV:05007, alleging that the Company, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, and the Company’s Chief Financial Officer violated the federal securities laws (the “Securities Action”). The complaint seeks to bring a class action on behalf of all persons and entities that purchased or otherwise acquired Company securities between July 7, 2022 and May 10, 2024. The complaint alleges that the defendants violated federal securities laws by issuing false, misleading, and/or omissive disclosures concerning the Company’s alleged lack of effective internal controls regarding the identification and review of impairment indicators for investments in real estate and the Company’s value and projected gross proceeds of certain real estate assets. The complaint seeks compensatory damages in an unspecified amount to be proven at trial, an award of reasonable costs and expenses to the plaintiff and class counsel, and such other and further relief as the court may deem just and proper. On or around January 15, 2025, another purported shareholder of the Company filed a derivative lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland, captioned Paul Sidhu v. Seritage Growth Properties, Case No. 1:25-cv-00152 (the “Sidhu Derivative Action”). On or around January 20, 2025, another purported shareholder of the Company filed a derivative lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland, captioned James Wallen v. Seritage Growth Properties, Case No. 1:25-cv-00190 (the “Wallen Derivative Action”). On or around May 8, 2025, another purported shareholder of the Company filed a derivative lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, captioned Derrick Cheroti v. Seritage Growth Properties, Case No. 1:25-vc-00152 (the “Cheroti Derivative Action”). The derivative actions allege the same or similar claimed acts and omissions underlying the Securities Action, assert breach of fiduciary duty and other claims against the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, the Company’s Chief Financial Officer, and current and former members of the Company’s Board of Trustees, and name the Company as a nominal defendant. The complaint in each of the derivative actions seeks compensatory damages in an unspecified amount to be proven at trial, an order directing the Company and the individual defendants to reform and improve the Company’s corporate governance and internal procedures, restitution from the individual defendants, an award of costs and expenses to the plaintiff and reasonable attorneys’ and experts’ fees, costs, and expenses, and such other and further relief as the court may deem just and proper. The complaint in the Cheroti Derivative Action also seeks an award of punitive damages, an order directing the individual defendants to account for all damages caused by them and all profits and special benefits and unjust enrichment obtained, and the imposition of a constructive trust. On September 2, 2025, the court in the Cheroti Derivative Action stayed the Cheroti Derivative Action until resolution of the anticipated motion to dismiss in the Securities Action. On November 5, 2025, the court in the District of Maryland proceedings consolidated the Sidhu Derivative Action and the Wallen Derivative Action (the “Consolidated Derivative Action”) and appointed lead counsel. On November 12, 2025, the court in the Consolidated Derivative Action stayed the Consolidated Derivative Action until resolution of the anticipated motion to dismiss in the Securities Action. The Company intends to vigorously defend itself against the allegations in these lawsuits.

Strategic Review

At the 2022 Annual Meeting of Shareholders on October 24, 2022, Seritage shareholders approved the Company’s Plan of Sale. The strategic review process remains ongoing as the Company executes the Plan of Sale, and the Company remains open-minded to pursuing value-maximizing alternatives, including a potential sale of the Company. There can be no assurance regarding the success of the process.

Market Update

The Company continues to face challenging market conditions, such as elevated interest rates and the availability of debt and equity capital, and it continues to assess other potential macroeconomic impacts including supply chain issues, international conflicts associated with tariffs, potential labor issues, and uncertainty caused by wars and the impacts thereof. Interest rates are currently higher than interest rates in 2022. Additionally, raising equity capital for land development deals remains challenging. These conditions could apply downward pricing pressures on our remaining assets. In making decisions regarding whether and when to transact on each of the Company’s remaining assets, the Company considers various factors including, but not limited to, the breadth of the buyer universe, macroeconomic conditions including the availability and cost of financing, as well as corporate, operating and other capital expenses required to carry the asset. If these challenging market conditions persist, then we expect that they will continue to adversely impact the Plan of Sale proceeds from our assets and the amounts and timing of distributions to shareholders.

Forward-looking statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, assumptions and contingencies, many of which are beyond the Company’s control, which may cause actual results to differ significantly from those expressed in any forward-looking statement. Factors that could cause or contribute to such differences include, but are not limited to: declines in retail, real estate and general economic conditions; risks relating to redevelopment activities and disposition of properties; the process and results of the Company’s review of strategic alternatives and our Plan of Sale; to contingencies to the commencement of rent under leases; the terms of the Company’s indebtedness and other legal requirements to which the Company is subject; competition and related challenges in the real estate and retail industries and the ability of the Company’s top tenants to successfully operate their businesses; failure to achieve expected occupancy and/or rent levels within the projected time frame or at all; the impact of ongoing negative operating cash flow on the Company’s ability to fund operations and ongoing development; the Company’s ability to access or obtain sufficient sources of financing to fund the Company’s liquidity needs; environmental, health, safety and land use laws and regulations; and possible acts of war, terrorist activity or other acts of violence or cybersecurity incidents. About Seritage Growth Properties

Prior to the adoption of the Company’s Plan of Sale, Seritage was principally engaged in the ownership, development, redevelopment, management, sale and leasing of diversified retail and mixed-use properties throughout the United States. As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s portfolio consisted of interests in eight properties comprised of approximately 0.7 million square feet of gross leasable area (“GLA”) or build-to-suit leased area and 133 acres of land. The portfolio encompasses three consolidated properties consisting of approximately 0.2 million square feet of GLA and 51 acres (such properties, the “Consolidated Properties”) and five unconsolidated entities consisting of approximately 0.5 million square feet of GLA and 82 acres (such properties, the “Unconsolidated Properties”).

data.title: Cingulate Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Regulatory Update on CTx-1301 NDA Resubmission
data.description:
Manufacturing Work Addressing FDA CMC Information Requests Substantially Completed

NDA Resubmission Expected Between December 2026 and January 2027

KANSAS CITY, Kan., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cingulate Inc. , a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) drug delivery platform to develop a pipeline of next-generation products, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and announced that it has substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) information requests for CTx-1301. The Company expects to resubmit the new drug application (NDA) for CTx-1301 between December 2026 and January 2027.

“With the manufacturing work substantially complete, we are now finalizing the data and documentation needed to resubmit the NDA for CTx-1301, and we expect to do so by January 2027, potentially sooner,” stated Cingulate Chairman and CEO Shane J. Schaffer. “Importantly, the FDA’s Complete Response Letter did not raise any concerns about the clinical safety or efficacy of CTx-1301. We thank our shareholders for their patience and continued support as we work to bring this treatment to patients with ADHD.”

Regulatory Update: CTx-1301 NDA Resubmission Progress

On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) for the CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) NDA. The CRL identified specific requests for additional CMC information and did not identify any concerns regarding the clinical safety or efficacy of CTx-1301, the Company’s lead ADHD asset.

Since then, Cingulate and its contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO), Bend Bioscience, have substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests in the CRL and are finalizing the supporting data and documentation for resubmission. As announced on November 9, 2026, the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2027. After the FDA receives the resubmission, it is expected to classify it as a Class 1 or Class 2 resubmission, which carry review goals of two and six months, respectively.

Third Quarter Financial Results

Cash and Working Capital: As of September 30, 2026, Cingulate had approximately $23.2 million in cash and cash equivalents, compared to $11.0 million as of December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by capital raised during the first nine months of 2026, including the close of a $12.0 million private placement in the first quarter and $22.5 million of capital raised on Cingulate’s At-the-Market Agreement with AGP and Purchase Agreement with Lincoln Park Capital, partially offset by $20.4 million in cash used for operations. As of September 30, 2026, Cingulate had approximately $18.8 million in working capital, an increase of $16.1 million as compared to December 31, 2025.

Under its current business plan, the Company believes its cash and cash equivalents will be sufficient to fund operations into mid-2027, including costs associated with seeking regulatory approval for CTx-1301, and continuing the build-out of commercial readiness capabilities.

R&D Expenses: Research and development expenses were $2.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 2.2% from $2.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, driven primarily by higher drug manufacturing costs to address the CMC information requested in the FDA’s CRL, partially offset by lower clinical operations costs following the conclusion of clinical study activities in early 2025, the absence of regulatory costs incurred in the prior-year period in connection with preparing the CTx-1301 NDA, and lower personnel expenses. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, R&D expenses were $6.6 million, a decrease of 15.3% from $7.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, driven primarily by lower clinical operations and regulatory costs, partially offset by increased manufacturing activities related to CTx-1301 following the CRL.

SG&A Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses (SG&A) were $4.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 45.5%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, SG&A expenses were $14.2 million, compared to $6.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 116.6%. The increases were driven primarily by the build-out of commercial readiness capabilities, including increased headcount and expanded market access, pricing, reimbursement and medical affairs activity conducted through Indegene, the Company’s commercialization partner.

Net Loss: Net loss was $7.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net loss was $22.9 million, compared to $16.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases primarily reflect the higher SG&A expenses described above, partially offset in the third quarter by a smaller loss from the change in fair value of derivative and lower interest expense, and for the nine-month period by lower R&D expenses.

About Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

ADHD is a chronic neurobiological and developmental disorder that affects millions of children and often continues into adulthood. The estimated market size of the US ADHD market is approximately 100 million annual prescriptions. The condition is marked by an ongoing pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development. In the U.S., over 20 million patients have been diagnosed with ADHD. Among this group, 12 million are adults and over 8 million are under the age of 17. According to the CDC, just 53.6 percent of all children and teens with ADHD reported they were actively treating their symptoms with medication in 2022, with 65-90 percent demonstrating clinical ADHD symptoms that persist into adulthood. Current market trends demonstrate that adult ADHD prevalence is larger and growing faster than the child and adolescent segments combined.

About CTx-1301

CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) is a once-daily, multi-core tablet utilizing Cingulate’s proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) platform to deliver three precisely timed releases of active medication across the day. This design aims to provide rapid onset of effect and entire active-day duration. CTx-1301 is being evaluated for the treatment of ADHD under the FDA’s 505(b)(2) pathway. In October 2025, the FDA accepted for review the NDA for CTx-1301 and assigned a PDUFA target action date of May 31, 2026. On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for the CTx-1301 NDA; the Company and its CDMO have since substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests, and the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2026. There can be no assurance regarding the timing of any resubmission or whether approval will occur.

About Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) Platform Technology

Cingulate is developing ADHD and anxiety disorder product candidates capable of achieving true once-daily dosing using Cingulate’s innovative PTR drug delivery platform technology. It incorporates a proprietary Erosion Barrier Layer (EBL) providing control of drug release at precise, pre-defined times with no release of drug prior to the intended release. The EBL technology is enrobed around a drug-containing core to give a tablet-in-tablet dose form. It is designed to erode at a controlled rate until eventually the drug is released from the core tablet. The EBL formulation, Oralogik™, is licensed from BDD Pharma. Cingulate intends to utilize its PTR technology to expand and augment its clinical-stage pipeline by identifying and developing additional product candidates in other therapeutic areas in addition to Anxiety and ADHD.

About Cingulate Inc.

Cingulate Inc. is a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary PTR drug delivery platform technology to build and advance a pipeline of next-generation pharmaceutical products, designed to improve the lives of patients suffering from frequently diagnosed conditions characterized by burdensome daily dosing regimens and suboptimal treatment outcomes. With an initial focus on the treatment of ADHD, Cingulate is identifying and evaluating additional therapeutic areas where PTR technology may be employed to develop future product candidates, including to treat anxiety disorders. Cingulate is headquartered in Kansas City. For more information, visit Cingulate.com.

data.title: Clean Seed And Wetaskiwin Co-Op Showcase Smart Seeder Mini-Max™ At Agri-Trade 2026
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    VANCOUVER, BRITISH COLUMBIA – November 13, 2026 – TheNewswire - Clean Seed Capital Group Ltd. (“Clean Seed” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce it participated alongside Wetaskiwin Co-op at the Agri-Trade Equipment Expo, taking place November 11–13, 2026, at Westerner Park in Red Deer, Alberta.

    The Company’s SMART Seeder Mini-MAX™ is being showcased through the commercial dealer and distribution relationship previously announced with Wetaskiwin Co-op, representing an important step in the introduction of Clean Seed’s precision seeding technology to agricultural producers throughout Central Alberta.

    The joint participation at Agri-Trade brings the Mini-MAX directly to one of Western Canada’s major agricultural equipment exhibitions, providing an opportunity for producers to see the technology, learn about its capabilities and engage with the organizations working together to bring it to market.

    Advancing the Wetaskiwin Co-op Relationship

    Under the commercial dealer and distribution relationship announced September 17, 2026, Wetaskiwin Co-op is working with Clean Seed to promote and sell the SMART Seeder Mini-MAX™ to farmers throughout Central Alberta.

    The relationship with Wetaskiwin provides Clean Seed with access to an established agricultural customer base and an experienced local cooperative with longstanding relationships throughout the farming community.

    Agri-Trade represents an important opportunity to advance these efforts, build awareness of Mini-MAX and develop direct sales opportunities as producers consider their equipment requirements for the upcoming growing season.

    Wetaskiwin Co-op is a member-owner of Federated Co-operatives Limited (FCL), one of Canada’s largest cooperative organizations. FCL’s network includes more than 150 independent retail cooperatives across Western Canada, representing a potential longer-term opportunity for Clean Seed to expand its Canadian market presence.

    Bringing Precision Seeding Technology to More Farmers

    The SMART Seeder Mini-MAX™ was developed to bring Clean Seed’s patented precision seeding architecture to a wider range of agricultural operations.

    Available in compact configurations beginning at five feet, with planned configurations extending up to 20 feet, Mini-MAX is designed to provide producers with advanced precision seed and fertilizer metering, multiple-product delivery and row-by-row application control.

    Clean Seed Executive Commentary

    Graeme Lempriere, Founder, Chairman & CEO of Clean Seed, commented:

    “We are very pleased to have participated at Agri-Trade alongside Wetaskiwin Co-op and to see the Mini-MAX being introduced directly to Alberta producers.

    Our relationship with Wetaskiwin Co-op is an important step in our efforts to expand the commercial availability of Mini-MAX in Canada. We recognize the value of working with established agricultural organizations that have strong relationships with their farming communities, and we appreciate the commitment and efforts of the Wetaskiwin team in helping bring this technology to market.

    Our objective is to put the Mini-MAX in front of farmers, demonstrate what the technology can offer and build a sustainable equipment business together. We see considerable opportunity in this relationship and believe a successful introduction in Central Alberta could provide a foundation for further expansion within the broader Co-op network.

    We are grateful for this partnership with Wetaskiwin Co-op and look forward to building on the momentum together.”

    About Clean Seed Capital Group Ltd.

    Clean Seed is an agricultural technology company commercializing its award-winning, internationally patented SMART Seeder™ technologies. Designed for real-world conditions and backed by independent field trials, these tools reduce fertilizer usage while supporting higher crop performance and overall farm profitability.

    At the heart of Clean Seed’s product line is the SMART Seeder™ system—a breakthrough in precision seeding that combines advanced electronic metering with intuitive software control. Its ability to deliver row-by-row variable rate inputs positions it as a leading innovation in the next generation of sustainable farming.

    Clean Seed is partnered with Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd., the world’s largest tractor manufacturer by volume, strengthening its global path to market and large-scale adoption.

    The common shares of Clean Seed Capital Group Ltd. are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and trade under the symbol "CSX".

data.title: Millicom To Acquire Entel Peru For $1.714 Bln
data.description:
LUXEMBOURG (dpa-AFX) - On Friday, Millicom International Cellular S.A. (TIGO) agreed to acquire Entel Peru for $1.714 billion, including lease liabilities, at 5 times its estimated 2026 EBITDA. The acquisition will be funded through local financing and cash reserves.

The payment will be made in three installments: 65% at closing, 10% after 12 months, and 25% after 18 months.

The deal is expected to close in early December 2026, subject to customary conditions.

On Nasdaq, the shares for Millicom are trading at $79.33 in the after hours. The shares closed Friday's regular trading 1.86 percent down.
